newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - CSL says to keep seeking investments.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - CSL says to keep seeking investments.

text.p: Vaccine and blood products manufacturer CSL Ltd said on Thursday that it would continue to seek investment opportunities to cement its domestic and international growth and it looks to the future with confidence.

"We will continue to seek investment opportunities in major markets, and cement our growth domestically and internationally," managing director Brian McNamee said at the annual meeting. Last month, CSL formed a joint venture with Sweden's Astra AB to develop a vaccine to treat ulcers and stomach cancers.
McNamee said that in terms of furture directions, CSL would maintain focus on the quality of returns, as measured in growth of earnings per share and cash flow generation.

He said an integral part of its future strategy was maintaining a focussed research and development (R&D) programme, developing new value adding intellectual property and teaming up with the appropriate partners to develop these opportunities.
"We look forward to the future prospects of the company with every confidence," McNamee said.
CSL reported an 18 percent rise in net profit to A$29 million for the year to June 30.

CSL chairman Colin Harper told shareholders the cut in the R&D tax concession to 125 percent from 150 percent in the 1996/97 federal budget could spell the end of the government's "Factor (f)" pharmaceutical industry funding scheme.

"Two such cuts, in our tax deduction and potentially in Factor (f), will require your company to run even faster than we currently are to make progress which we wish to achieve," Harper said. At 12.10 p.m. (0110 GMT), CSL shares were eight cents or 1.21 percent lower at A$6.52.
